headline: Large Energy Users Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill directs Virginia's primary electric provider to petition the State Corporation Commission (SCC) to establish rates that recover the costs of increasing electric generating capacity from customers with 25 MW or more in electric demand, effectively requiring data centers and other large energy users to pay for the cost of increasing capacity.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Senator Mark Warner, Senator Louise Lucas, environmental advocates.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by shifting expenses to data centers
news_summary: A Virginia bill aims to cut residential energy costs by requiring data centers to shoulder more of the electrical infrastructure costs. If passed, residential rates could drop, while data center costs would increase significantly.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting Mandate
short_summary: This legislation requires water suppliers to report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing better data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Senator Kannan Srinivasan, Delegate Elizabeth Guzman, Delegate Shelly Simonds, environmental groups, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: Virginia Lawmakers Approve Legislation to Track Water Use by Data Centers Across Virginia
news_summary: The Virginia General Assembly passed SB 553, requiring water suppliers to report water volumes provided to data centers. This legislation aims to strengthen water-use reporting and provide better data on the industry's impact on Virginia's water resources.

headline: Local Data Center Siting and Noise Rules
short_summary: This bill requires localities to make applicants for new high energy use facilities, such as data centers, submit a site assessment examining sound profiles and other potential impacts before approving rezoning or permits.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0567) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data centers, environmental and conservation groups, local planning and public health organizations.
opponents: Data center developers, tech industry trade groups, chambers of commerce, commercial real estate associations, pro-growth business or utility groups.
news_headline: Data centers; site assessment, sound profile of the high energy use facility.
news_summary: This bill requires Virginia localities to mandate site assessments for new data centers exceeding 100 megawatts, focusing on sound profiles and impacts on nearby homes and schools. Localities can also require reviews on water, agricultural, and historic resources.
